acceptance: The owner's decision for #4384, #4385 and the normalizer branch is recorded and carried out.
context: Filed 2026-11-20 from the adversarial review of the scale-factor and TPC-DI remediation work (PRs #4298-#4385 and benchbox-site #178-#210).
description:
## Problem
The redesign rested on the claim that baseline refresh pull requests never land. 6 of 10 `chore/fast-baseline-*` pull requests merged, with a longest gap of 8 days; scheduled ones were simply not merged. Review found: the unopened branch `feat/fast-duration-gate-normalization-and-refresh` lets a pull request change the collection time its own timings are divided by (a 40% slowdown passes if collection also slows 40%), stops charging new tests in untouched files, accepts failed runs as baseline sources and rescales the baseline up 3.7%; #4385 makes a file a blocking gate reads unreviewed, its `reproduce` job never ran in CI and refreshes would still need a person because of the unattributed-commit rule; #4384 states runner noise as the cause without establishing it.

## Change
Options, none preselected: close #4384 and #4385 unmerged and delete the normalizer branch and the two stacked branches; or keep and repair any of them. Closing reverses the owner's 2026-11-19 choices (the machine-checked exemption for refresh pull requests, and 'then implement B+C'). The same decision settles whether to drop fast-duration-baseline-scheduled-refresh-never-lands-20261119 and fast-duration-gate-scales-wait-bound-tests-by-cpu-factor-20261119, and where the criteria moved out of ci-fast-duration-gate-rerun-and-baseline-drift-20261113 now live. If #4384 is kept, file a repair item for its three findings (false stacking claim, unestablished cause, serial artifact reads).

## Decision gates
Blocked until the owner confirms closing each of the three. Closing pull requests and deleting remote branches are hosted writes that need the owner's word.

## Verification rubric
Pass: each named pull request is closed with a comment giving the reason, and the branches are deleted, or the owner's different instruction is recorded.

## Guardrails
- Any limit, default, threshold or label id or text is shown to the owner before it is committed. Briefs quote owner answers verbatim; questions to the owner carry no preselected answer.
- The implementer replies on review threads and leaves resolving them to the reviewer or the owner, unless the owner says otherwise (AGENTS.md asks agents to resolve benchbox-oracle threads on soundness paths; the owner has been asked which applies).
- Hosted writes (merge, close, disable or enable auto-merge, workflow dispatch, remote branch delete) only as the repository's close-out procedure or the owner's word for that pull request allows; never raw `gh pr merge` in core.
- No polling loop around `make pr-arm`, no `--no-verify`, no stand-in review unless the owner names the PR and head unprompted. Push only after `make pr-preflight` exits 0 on the exact head.
- No worktree takeover while another session may be working; no tracker write from a server that reports a stale version; never chain `git stash` with `git stash pop`.
- Heavy work runs only through `make heavy-run` or a lock-taking entry point, one run at a time.
- Status reports state only what merged and what was verified, with the evidence.
